title: Add success/duration logging to alert providers and config loader
description: Alert providers (discord, sendgrid, twilio) are missing success logs and duration tracking. twilio.go sendSMS has zero logging for the actual HTTP call. config.go Load() is silent about resolved configuration. docker/client.go has 4 minor gaps (Ping, Info, DiskUsage no logging, RestartContainer missing duration). Low priority sensitive data notes: discord webhook URL could leak via HTTP errors, twilio raw response body in error wrapping.

title: Add automated rollback on deploy failure
description: Flux supports automated rollback on Helm install/upgrade failure. Bosun has backup-before-deploy (timestamped tar.gz) but no mechanism to automatically restore from backup when compose up fails. Add optional rollback that restores the previous backup and runs compose up again. See docs/gitops-comparison.md gap analysis.

title: Implement story pattern (begin/success/fail) logging
close_reason: Story pattern (begin/success/fail) implemented in docker/client.go, reconcile/deploy.go, reconcile/git.go, manifest/render.go, alert/alert.go with timing and error context

title: Standardize config loading patterns
close_reason: Config loading pattern established: config.Load() as main entry, loadConfigFile/loadXConfig helpers for subsystems, env var overrides. Used consistently in config.go and daemon.go

title: Reduce compose up blast radius with per-service granularity
description: ComposeUpMultiple feeds all compose files with --remove-orphans. If one service in core.yml has a bad image tag, the whole stack fails. For a homelab with 10-20 containers, this means one broken service takes down compose up for everything. Rollback restores configs and re-runs compose up (correct), but the blast radius is the entire stack. Investigate per-service or per-file compose up strategies, ordered by dependency. The --wait flag helps catch health failures but doesn't reduce blast radius.

title: lock and snapshot packages use Unix-only syscalls without build tags
description: internal/lock/lock.go uses syscall.Flock (Unix-only) and internal/snapshot/snapshot.go uses syscall.Statfs_t/Statfs (Unix-only), but neither file has build tags. The reconcile package correctly handles this with lock_unix.go and lock_windows.go. These packages will fail to compile on Windows.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/low-hanging-fruit branch

title: Add structured logging to manifest template rendering
close_reason: Added structured logging to RenderService and RenderStack with provision loading and error tracking

title: Add graceful shutdown support for containers with configurable timeout
description: Add the ability to gracefully stop containers with a configurable timeout before force-killing. Docker's default SIGTERM->SIGKILL flow should be exposed through bosun so operators can control how long containers get to drain connections and clean up. Key considerations: configurable timeout per-container or globally, honor Docker's stop_grace_period if set in compose, sensible default (e.g. 30s), progress feedback during shutdown wait.
notes: Guide created at docs/guides/graceful-shutdown.md covering 6 layers: buy time (config), signal clients (app code), blue-green (infra), preemptive draining (readiness probes), dependency-aware shutdown order, and checkpoint/resume for long-running jobs.

title: Legacy Python pyproject.toml created in init wizard
description: internal/cmd/init.go lines 149-153: The init wizard creates a pyproject.toml file as part of project scaffolding. This is a legacy artifact from when bosun was a Python project. Bosun is now a Go binary and pyproject.toml is misleading.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add OpenTelemetry tracing
description: Flux v2.7 added OTel tracing for reconciliation spans. Bosun has correlation IDs (request_id, reconcile_id) but no trace propagation. Add OpenTelemetry span instrumentation to the reconciliation pipeline. Correlation IDs already exist as a foundation. See docs/gitops-comparison.md gap analysis.

title: Add drift ignore rules
description: Argo CD supports ignoreDifferences per application to suppress known noise in drift detection. Bosun has no equivalent. Add configurable ignore patterns for drift detection (e.g., ignore specific container labels, environment variables, or fields that change frequently). See docs/gitops-comparison.md gap analysis.

title: N+1 ContainerInspect calls in ListContainers for health status
description: internal/docker/client.go: ListContainers calls ContainerInspect once per container to get health status. With many containers this causes N+1 API calls. Should use the docker API list options to include health status in the initial list response, or batch the inspect calls.
close_reason: Closed

title: Validate paths in template include function
description: The include template function in reconcile reads arbitrary files with no path validation: a template could {{ include "/etc/shadow" }}. Current threat model is fine since templates come from a trusted repo, but if Bosun ever processes templates from untrusted sources this is an arbitrary file read. Add path validation to restrict includes to within the source directory tree. Low priority since the threat model is personal repo only.

title: Architectural ceiling: legacy and helm format paths are mutually exclusive
description: Config.Format() returns 'helm' or 'legacy' based on filesystem structure — no mixed mode. runProvision switches to two completely separate functions. You cannot have a stack that references both charts and legacy provisions. Migration must be completed in one shot or you maintain two repos. Breaking this requires a common Renderer interface with LegacyRenderer and ChartRenderer implementations, and per-entry format dispatch in stacks. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Handle remote deploy partial failure: config synced but compose up fails
description: Remote deploy uses SSH for both config sync (rsync) and compose up. If SSH succeeds for config sync but fails during compose up, configs on disk are ahead of running containers. State file correctly does NOT record success, but the remote host has new configs that aren't running. Next reconcile sees no git change and may skip. Need to either: (1) track config-synced-but-not-applied state, (2) always re-run compose up if last attempt failed, or (3) verify running state matches deployed configs post-deploy.

title: Architectural ceiling: single reconcile queue with coalescing
description: Daemon has one pendingTrigger bool and one triggerSource string. Multiple concurrent triggers collapse into at most one pending run. No priority queue, no per-source queueing, no fast-path for lightweight operations (container restart) vs full reconcile. A webhook arrives during a slow poll reconcile and must wait for the full pipeline to complete. Breaking this requires a typed work queue with priority and different execution modes. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Add input validation to webhook handlers

title: Investigate per-file code review for large PRs

Filed upstream: anthropics/claude-code#25662. If upstream doesn't fix, consider: (1) custom review prompt that uses gh api to fetch per-file diffs, (2) splitting workflow to review changed files individually, (3) accept limitation for large PRs.

title: Hand-rolled JSON output in printStatusJSON instead of encoding/json
description: internal/cmd/status.go lines 126-153: printStatusJSON manually constructs JSON via string concatenation with a custom escapeJSON helper function. This is error-prone (missing escapes, wrong structure). Should use encoding/json.Marshal or a struct with json tags.
close_reason: Closed

title: Architectural ceiling: shallow clone breaks DiffFiles for post-sync hooks
description: Git clone and fetch both use depth=1. DiffFiles calls repo.CommitObject(fromHash) but the previous commit stored in state may be pruned from the shallow clone. When bosun is down for multiple commits, DiffFiles silently fails with a warning and skips ALL hook execution. Post-sync container restarts don't fire. Breaking this requires either configurable fetch depth, a fallback that treats all files as changed when from-commit is unavailable, or switching to full clones. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Add force flag to daemon trigger API
description: TriggerRequest only has Source field. Webhooks and API triggers cannot force re-deployment when git state is already up-to-date but deployment was interrupted. Need to add Force bool to TriggerRequest, thread it through TriggerReconcile to reconcile.Config.Force, and expose via CLI (bosun trigger --force), socket API, TCP API, and webhook API.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #27

title: Add post-sync container restart hooks for config-watching services

Use git diff between deployed commits to detect changed files. Generalizes to Prometheus, Grafana, Gatus, nginx. Ref: openspec changes/add-deploy-resilience, GitHub #38

title: validateStackFile always returns true (validation is a no-op)
description: internal/cmd/diagnostics.go: validateStackFile always returns true regardless of input. The function body only returns true with no actual validation logic. This means the doctor/lint commands silently pass invalid stack files.
close_reason: Closed

title: Architectural ceiling: health endpoint is binary with no subsystem breakdown
description: /health returns a single 'healthy' or 'degraded' status based on one lastError field. No per-subsystem breakdown (git, template, deploy, drift). A drift alert puts daemon in 'degraded' even though it can deploy fine. A watchdog would restart a functional daemon over a transient git failure. Breaking this requires a richer HealthStatus model with named subsystems, per-stage outcomes from executeReconcile, and a severity-graded aggregate. This is a breaking API change. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Architectural ceiling: daemon is single-repo
description: Daemon watches exactly one git repository. ConfigFromEnv reads a single REPO_URL. NewReconciler accepts one RepoURL. Run() calls git.Sync() singular. Multi-repo setups (e.g. networking stack in one repo, media stack in another) require running N daemon processes. Breaking this requires ReconcileConfig becoming a slice, per-repo clone dirs and state files, and webhook routing per repo. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

close_reason: Added logging for individual SMS failures and partial delivery summary in twilio.go Send method

title: Config file parsed independently 4 times on startup
description: internal/config/config.go: The config file is read and parsed 4 separate times via loadConfigFile, loadInfraContainers, loadTunnelConfig, and loadAlertConfig. Each does independent file I/O and YAML parsing. Should parse once and extract sections from the parsed structure.
close_reason: Closed

title: Architectural ceiling: per-chart template namespaces don't exist
description: All charts share a single charts/templates/ directory. Two charts can't both define container.yaml with different behavior. Charts are not self-contained packages — they depend on project-level shared templates. Additionally, chart dependencies resolve to templates (not full sub-charts), and stack values bleed into all charts with no scoping. Breaking this requires: (1) search-path resolution in TemplateEngine (chart-local then project-level), (2) ChartLoader/TemplateEngine mutual coupling for sub-chart dependency resolution, (3) namespaced value schema for stacks. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Sentry: use atomic.Bool for state.enabled to prevent data race

title: Architectural ceiling: config is load-once, no hot-reload

Changing REPO_URL, POLL_INTERVAL, WEBHOOK_SECRET, or any config requires full daemon restart, which interrupts polling and loses the pending-trigger queue. Breaking this requires atomic config reads, SIGHUP handler, and decoupling config from construction. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Make deploy paths data-driven instead of hardcoded
description: deployLocal and deployRemote have hardcoded sync targets (traefik, authelia, agentgateway, gatus, tailscale-gateway, compose — 6 paths). Adding a new service requires a code change to Bosun. The manifest/provision system is generic but the deploy step collapses to an explicit list. This is the root cause of error pages and one-shot-apps not deploying. The deploy step needs to become data-driven: either a deploy manifest in the repo that declares what directories to sync, or auto-discovery of directories in the rendered output. This is the single biggest gap between 'GitOps for Cameron' and 'GitOps for Docker Compose'.

title: Add panic recovery to daemon background goroutines

A panic in any of these crashes the daemon silently without reporting to Sentry. Add defer sentrypkg.Recover() to each goroutine spawned in Run().

description: internal/cmd/webhook.go line 293 validates GitLab tokens with plain string comparison (token != h.secret) instead of crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare. This is susceptible to timing attacks that could leak the secret token byte-by-byte. The TCP server already uses constant-time comparison correctly (internal/daemon/tcp.go).
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace stderr writes with structured logging in snapshot

title: Add generic webhook alert provider

This would enable integration with any service that accepts webhooks without needing a dedicated provider. See docs/gitops-comparison.md gap analysis.

title: Architectural ceiling: provision/template lookup is filesystem-only
description: Every load operation (provisions, templates, charts, values) is a raw os.ReadFile call with no abstraction. Cannot reference provisions from a URL, OCI registry, or central Git repo. Every project must copy-paste provisions locally. Community provision sharing across multiple yachts is impossible. Breaking this requires a Source/Loader interface (FilesystemSource, HTTPSource, GitSource) threaded through LoadProvision, ChartLoader, and TemplateEngine. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Image update policy: auto vs pinned per-service
description: Add per-service image update policy so Bosun can own both config AND image updates. Two strategies: (1) pinned — Bosun deploys exactly what Git declares, updates only on version bump commits. (2) auto — Bosun runs docker compose pull before compose up for services tagged auto, pulling mutable tags like :latest. This replaces Watchtower for Bosun-managed services and closes the gap where two update mechanisms (Watchtower + Bosun) don't know about each other. Implementation: conditional pull before ComposeUpMultiple based on policy, configurable per-service in compose templates or bosun.yaml.

title: Architectural ceiling: grace period blocks reconcile lock
description: Post-deploy verification sleeps for StartupGracePeriod (default 30s) inside Run(), which holds the flock. During this window, webhook triggers queue but can't execute. Rapid iteration gets a 30s hard floor on reconcile throughput. Breaking this requires extracting verification from Run() hot path and running it asynchronously after lock release, with careful state coordination for DriftCheckedAt/DriftItems. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Add structured logging to tunnel providers (cloudflare, tailscale)
description: Both tunnel provider implementations have ZERO logging across 10 combined external calls (6 cloudflare, 4 tailscale). subprocess executions, HTTP calls, and error paths are all silent. Add structured logging with component=tunnel, operation names, duration_ms, and start/success/failure for each external call.

Aligns with project observability standards (structured logging + OpenTelemetry + error tracking).

title: Architectural ceiling: drift detection is Docker-local only
description: CollectActualState calls client.ListContainers via the local Docker socket. docker.NewClient() creates a local-only client. For remote deploys (SSH+rsync to another host), post-deploy drift verification is completely blind — the Docker daemon on the target host is unreachable. This is the primary deployment scenario (bosun in container on NAS, deploying to Unraid). Breaking this requires DockerClientFunc to support remote Docker endpoints (DOCKER_HOST, Docker-over-SSH, TLS). See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

close_reason: Added sync.Mutex to protect file field in Lock struct, Acquire and Release now thread-safe for concurrent goroutine access

title: Track last successfully deployed commit persistently
description: Bosun detects 'no changes' by comparing git HEAD before/after fetch. If a deployment is interrupted mid-way (e.g., daemon restart during webhook processing), the git state is already updated but deployment never completed. On next trigger, bosun sees no git changes and skips deployment entirely. Need persistent state tracking (small file) that records the last commit hash that was fully rendered AND deployed. On startup or trigger, compare against this rather than just git diff. This catches interrupted deployments and automatically re-runs them.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #27

title: Add structured logging to destructive CLI commands (yacht down/restart, crew restart)

Should follow the pattern established by emergency.go: log.Warn() before, log.Error() on failure, log.Warn() after, with FieldOperation and FieldContainer. Also minor gaps in comms.go, status.go, and render.go error paths.

title: Add Prometheus metrics endpoint

Expose metrics at /metrics endpoint covering: reconciliation count/duration, drift detection results, alert dispatch success/failure, daemon uptime, active connections. See docs/gitops-comparison.md gap analysis.

title: Architectural ceiling: webhook handler is GitHub-only
description: Only /webhook/github has structured payload parsing with branch filtering and HMAC signature verification. GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, and Bitbucket must use the generic /webhook endpoint with no signature validation and no branch filtering. Common for homelabs running self-hosted Gitea/Forgejo. Breaking this requires a WebhookProvider interface with Verify() and ParsePush() methods, a provider registry, and route registration driven by config. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Architectural ceiling: single-target reconciler
description: The reconciler is structurally limited to one target per instance. Config has one TargetHost, one StateFile, one StagingDir, one ProjectName. The daemon holds one Reconciler. Multi-server ('one yacht, many ports') requires running N separate daemon processes with no coordination. Related sub-ceilings: (1) state file is process-local, (2) single shared staging directory prevents concurrent reconciles, (3) secrets are flat-merged with no per-target scoping. Breaking this requires Config becoming a list of target descriptors, per-target state files, per-run staging directories, and namespaced secrets. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: SSH InsecureIgnoreHostKey bypasses host key verification
description: internal/reconcile/git.go lines 115 and 142 use ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey() which disables SSH host key verification entirely. This makes git operations vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. Should use known_hosts file or at minimum warn the user. Security issue - P1.
close_reason: Added getHostKeyCallback() that searches known_hosts files (BOSUN_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS, ~/.ssh/known_hosts, /config/known_hosts) before falling back to insecure. BOSUN_SSH_INSECURE_HOST_KEY=true for explicit opt-out. All tests pass.

title: Architectural ceiling: output targets hardcoded to compose/traefik/gatus
description: RenderOutput is a concrete struct with three named fields (Compose, Traefik, Gatus). TargetNames is a package-level constant. Every merge, render, and write function has three explicit code paths. Adding a fourth output target (Prometheus scrape config, Nginx upstream, Caddy snippet) requires modifying type definitions and every function that touches them across the entire manifest package. Breaking this requires replacing concrete struct fields with map[string]map[string]any and making targets data-driven. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Sentry: mark context.Canceled spans as cancelled, not errored

title: Auth ingress kill switch: verify critical chain health post-deploy
description: After compose up, before marking deploy as success, verify the auth ingress chain (traefik, authelia, tailscale-gateway) is healthy. If any component is down, trigger rollback. A partial deploy where traefik is up but authelia is down is a silent security hole — open reverse proxy without auth middleware. The VerifyContainerHealth stub in reconcile.go is the right insertion point. Layered approach: compose depends_on for startup ordering, forwardAuth for runtime, and this post-deploy health gate for the reconciler.

title: Architectural ceiling: alert system is frozen and unroutable
description: Two related ceilings: (1) Alert providers are assembled at startup and frozen — no Add/Remove/Reload. Rotating a Discord webhook or silencing SMS during maintenance requires daemon restart. (2) No per-event routing — Manager.Send() iterates all providers unconditionally. Breaking this requires thread-safe provider mutations, SIGHUP-triggered reload, and a routing layer with {provider, filter} pairs. See docs/gitops-comparison.md.

title: Add structured logging to daemon API and webhook handlers
description: The daemon package has major logging gaps: api.go has ZERO logging across 6 handlers (383 lines), webhook handlers (server.go) have no processing logs, socket.go shutdown is silent, tcp.go auth failures are not logged. Also: ui.* used instead of structured log.* in 10+ locations, goroutine context loss breaks request-to-reconcile correlation. Includes auth failure logging (security-relevant).

title: Add structured logging to docker package
close_reason: Added structured logging to NewClient, ListContainers, RemoveContainer, RestartContainer, GetContainerLogs, and GetContainerStats

title: Add structured logging to reconcile git operations
close_reason: Added structured logging to Clone, Pull, and Sync operations with timing and commit info

title: Add drift self-healing mode
description: Argo CD (selfHeal: true) and Flux (interval-based re-apply) auto-correct drift. Bosun currently detects drift and alerts but does not auto-remediate. Add optional self-healing that triggers reconciliation when drift is detected. Should be opt-in with a config flag. See docs/gitops-comparison.md gap analysis.
